prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: 16:9 landscape game loading-screen background for Animal Factory Tactics, 2048x1152 composition.
Primary request: a beautiful painterly military-industrial retrofuturist loading screen, compatible with an illustrated tactical game.
Scene: a fictional mid-century command room built inside a converted factory. A substantial worn olive-green steel operations console occupies the right half: one large curved amber-phosphor CRT with an abstract tactical radar sweep and plateau contour map, small round analog gauges, chunky rotary controls, mechanical pushbuttons, a reel-to-reel data unit, vent slots and coiled telephone cables. Above and behind it, heavy structural steel, riveted panels, a few large pipes and dim industrial depth; a single restrained rusty red warning lamp. The machinery feels coherent, practical and heavy.
Composition: cinematic eye-level three-quarter view, strong simple readable silhouettes, full-bleed wide artwork. Keep the left 38 percent as a broad, quiet dark olive-charcoal wall area with subtle paint and very low-detail atmospheric shading, reserved for a separately rendered game title. Keep the bottom 16 percent dark and visually quiet across the full width for a real loading progress strip. Main visual interest is center-right; keep important shapes inside a five-percent safe margin. Avoid borders and mock device frames.
Style: accomplished hand-painted game illustration, visible angular brushwork, simplified large material planes with carefully placed small highlights, warm cream worn edges, chipped olive enamel, aged brass, charcoal rubber and dark gunmetal. Match the bright, crafted painterly surfaces of an animal-worker tactics game; readable and atmospheric rather than photorealistic. Amber CRT glow spills softly over the nearby console and contrasts with a cool deep green factory background.
Constraints: no people, no characters, no modern flat screens, no neon cyberpunk colors, no floating holograms, no slick vector UI, no weapons schematic. NO lettering, numbers, game logo, slogans, progress bar, watermark or readable labels anywhere: the UI and text will be added separately in code. No excessive grime or blown-out lights. The entire result is a finished painted background, not a multi-panel concept sheet.
notes: Original generated pixels copied unchanged. Typography, progress, states and controls are separate HTML/CSS. This is an art-study asset; gameplay loading integration is separate.
